extracted.intended_audience: beekeepers, homemakers, and lay readers interested in honey's culinary, medicinal, and veterinary uses
extracted.subtask_description: A 19th‑century practical manual describing honey origin, types, extraction methods, signs of quality and adulteration, storage, culinary recipes, medicinal prescriptions for humans, and veterinary remedies using honey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soorten (types of honey by harvest method)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Volgens de wijze, waarop de honig uit de bieënwoningen geoogst wordt, onderscheidt men _gepersten_, _uitgetrokken_ of _geslingerden_ honig, en honig in _raten_ of _sectiën_."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that pressed honey (gepersten) was traditional but produces mixtures with wax, pollen and dead bees and degrades quality; extracted/spun (uitgetrokken/geslingerden) honey obtained with a centrifugal 'honigslinger' yields very pure honey; honey sold in combs or sections (sectiën) using prepared wax ensures authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of using a honey extractor (honigslinger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the honigslinger: "De honigslinger is een werktuig, dat op de middelpuntvliedende kracht gesteund is."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows procedure: remove frames, brush bees off, uncap cells, set frames in the extractor and spin; after a few minutes honey is drawn without breaking combs or contaminating, and without touching by hand. Conclusion: extracted/sprung honey is worth more and preserves freshness, aroma, taste, and color better than pressed honey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honey in sections (honig in sectiën) as guarantee of authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of small frames (sectiën) with fresh wax wafers (maagdenwas) in which bees build cells and fill with honey; sold in natural state ensures real honey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended as practiced in England and America; buying honey in comb/sections almost guarantees genuine honey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour as indicator and its variability
rubrics_metrics.description: "De kleur, de smaak, de geur en andere eigenschappen des honigs verschillen volgens de planten, waarvan hij voortkomt." followed by specific color indications for many flowers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples: most fruit trees = white; cherry = golden yellow; mustard and sloe = as clear as water; linden = yellow or dark green; acacia = white‑green; meadow flowers = yellow‑green or light brown; red clover = very clear, straw or lemon yellow; pine = yellow‑brown or yellow‑green; buckwheat = dark brown. Also notes soil affects color (chalky soils give clearer honey). Warns it's difficult to determine exact floral source by color alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vervalsching (adulteration) — types of adulterants
rubrics_metrics.description: List of common adulterations: addition of water (up to ~33%), mixing with flour, starch sugar, saccharose or cane sugar, molasses, gelatin, dextrine, heavy mineral substances, and much false honey made from glucose; adulterated glucose honey often tinted with a little real honey for good smell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains dishonest dealers' methods and prevalence of cheap foreign honey being adulterated; emphasizes cheapness often implies fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests to detect adulteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple methods to detect falsification rather than chemical analysis: weight test, tea test for glucose, crystallization, dilution sediment test, and sensory familiarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: pure honey ~1400 g per liter vs water 1000 g—lighter than expected weight suggests excess water; tea test: put a spoon of honey in tea — pure honey leaves tea color unchanged, glucose‑adulterated honey darkens the tea; crystallization (granulation) generally indicates purity; if mixed with foreign matter, adding water may reveal sinking of flour/sediment; experienced consumers can tell adulterated from good honey by habit. Recommends chemical analysis as best but costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchasing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice: buyers should obtain good, pure, and unadulterated honey from beekeepers known for honesty; buy at honey markets organized by local Beekeepers' associations (Bond der Bieëntelers van Brabant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States confidence in association members and mentions expulsion for fraud; recommends avoiding cheap foreign honey and purchase from known trustworthy sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bewaring (storage) — containers and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: "De honig moet bewaard worden in glazen of blikken bokalen, in aarden potten of in kleine houten vaten. De zinken voorwerpen deugen niet om er honig in te bewaren."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store in a dry, well‑ventilated place; honey is hygroscopic (moisture‑absorbing), so avoid cellars or damp rooms; when storing long‑term, use airtight jars and ensure honey is fully ripe before sealing to avoid fermentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behaviour and remedies for crystallization and fermentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure honey crystallizes becoming whiter and harder; some honeys crystallize quickly (rapeseed and many fruit trees). If old honey becomes liquid and starts to ferment, recover by heating in a double pot (bain‑marie), skimming impurities, or fix by adding chalk and wood charcoal and warming the pot in water while stirring; settle and decant to remove impurities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never place honey directly on a fire (direct heating drives off delicate aroma and reduces it to syrup); use gentle heating methods to restore consistency and remove fermentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honig as food — general endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: History and general claims: honey regarded as pleasant, healthy, strengthening, easily digestible and better than sugar; regular honey consumers benefit healthwise; used on bread, in coffee, and as a spread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: honey on bread recommended, used in many European traditions; honey is used to make gingerbread, cakes, syrups, candies, cool drinks, beer, wine, grogs, vinegars, brandy, and various liqueurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honig als geneesmiddel (general medical endorsement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honey is recommended as a foremost medicine: good for people with weak stomachs, for diseases of mouth, throat and respiratory organs; used for bladder and kidney ailments, and topical for wounds, boils and burns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author disclaims not replacing doctors; presents honey as effective in mild ailments, preventive, and palliative in chronic/serious cases; will give practical prescriptions collected from various sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1º Tegen de aamborstigheid of moeilijke ademhaling (Prescription 1: For shortness of breath)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Meng eene once (bijna 29 grammen) ricinusolie met vier oncen honig. Neem er 's morgens en 's avonds eenen lepel van." (Newman.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dose: roughly 1 ounce castor oil + 4 ounces honey; take a spoonful morning and evening. Cited source: Newman.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2º Geneesmiddel tegen den hoest (Prescription 2: Against cough)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Neem gedurende den dag, alle twee uren, een koffielepel heeten honig; 's avonds neme men nog eenen eer men slapen gaat, en 's morgens een uur vóór het ontbijt eenen anderen. Als men er een weinig ganzevet bijmengt, wordt dit geneesmiddel krachtiger..." (Dennler.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration: a teaspoon of hot honey every two hours during the day, plus before bed and one hour before breakfast; optional addition of a little goose fat increases effectiveness for coughs and laryngitis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3º Honigsiroop als geneesmiddel tegen den hoest (Honey‑syrup for cough)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipe: cook a half pint chopped onions and 1 gill (13 cL) olive oil in a covered dish; strain and add 1 gill good honey; mix, bottle and take a small spoonful in the evening before bed or whenever cough is severe. (Newman.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation instructions and dosing: keep in well‑stopped bottle; take small spoonfuls in evenings and when cough intensifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4º Honigdranken tegen hoest, keelpijn enz. (Honey drinks for throat and cough)
rubrics_metrics.description: Warm drinks sweetened with honey (wine, cider, grog) cure sore throat, cough and can help prevent diphtheria—especially when taken on an empty stomach before bed. (Apiculteur.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: warm alcoholic or non‑alcoholic drinks sweetened with honey; suitable as preventive and palliative treatment for respiratory complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5º Geneesmiddel tegen de influenza (Prescription 5: For influenza)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infuse a handful of lime (linden) blossoms for half an hour in 4 cups boiling water; add 2 spoonfuls of pure honey per cup; drink warm and go to bed in a warmed room. (Rucher.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dose and method: linden infusion sweetened with honey, taken warm before bed; claimed fast recovery by next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6º Nog tegen de influenza (Historical note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes the long‑known usefulness of honey and its products for respiratory treatments and cites 1782 practice using honey‑based 'honigmee' to cure influenza. (Progrès Apicole.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical endorsement of honey mead (honigmee) as therapeutic in influenza.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7º Geneesmiddel voor eenen verouderden hoest (Prescription 7: For chronic cough)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix one pint spun/extracted honey, one pint linseed oil and as much brandy (whisky) as desired; take 3–4 times per day a spoonful. (Newman.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicated for old and long‑standing coughs, especially in elderly persons or neglected colds with hot skin and rapid pulse.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8º Geneesmiddel tegen de ziekten der ademingsorganen (Honey for vocalists and respiratory diseases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honey (because of formic acid) is excellent against hoarseness, cough, colds, influenza, bronchitis, and as a demulcent for throat ailments. Honey from pine is best. A useful drink: warm wine/cider/milk sweetened with honey and a small glass of kirsch. (Voirnot / Voirnot & Voirnot cited.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended for teachers, musicians and those who misuse their voice; regular use with plantain (weegbree) noted as healing in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9º Honigkandij met teer (honey candy with tar) for cough
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil two handfuls of green horehound (malva?) in 3/4 water until a quarter remains; strain, add a cup of honey, same amount sugar, a spoon of lard and a spoon of tar (goudron); cook until set; begin with a pea‑sized dose and increase. (Newman.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for cough relief; warn not to overcook so it doesn't become hard and brittle.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10º External poultice: honey with flour for ulcers, boils, warts
rubrics_metrics.description: For external use combine honey with flour to form a healing salve for boils, ulcers and warts. (Gois.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical application; presented as a simple, beneficial poultice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11º Gorgeldrank met honig tegen de keelpijn (Gargle with honey and sage for sore throat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil some sage leaves, strain, add a spoon of honey and a spoon of vinegar per cup and gargle; best remedy to remove mucus that prevents swallowing and causes sore throat. (Dennler.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: use as warm gargle; recommended for clearing mucus and soothing throat.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12º Ander geneesmiddel tegen de keelpijn (Warm wine/cider with honey before bed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drink in the evening before sleep a bowl of warm wine or sweetened cider mixed with honey. (L'Apiculteur.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple home remedy for sore throat—taken warm before going to bed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13º Middel tegen verkoudheden (cod liver oil, honey and lemon for colds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix 2 ounces cod liver oil, 2 ounces honey and 2 ounces lemon juice; take two teaspoons three times a day. (World Médical.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dietary/medicinal mix recommended to prevent/fight colds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14º Middel om de vermoeidheid te bestrijden (fatigue remedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infuse a hand of 'santorie' (santonica/centaury or gall?) in one‑third liter water, boil, add 2–3 spoons honey and drink warm before bed to induce rest and sweating. (L'Auxiliaire de L'Apiculteur.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to relieve fatigue and induce restful sleep; indicates gathering time and season for plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15º Middel tegen de slapeloosheid (for insomnia)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of best remedies: a bowl of warm milk sweetened with honey and a little grated roasted nutmeg. (L'Abeille et sa Culture.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taken at night to encourage sleep; simple household remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16º Geneesmiddel tegen de bleekzucht (anemia treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment in Denmark and Hanover: give pale young women exercise outdoors and have them eat honey; Lehman theorized that hepatic sugar deficiency causing anemia is remedied by honey. (Revue Internationale d'Apiculture.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported good results; presented as nutritional therapy for mild anemia.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17º Geneesmiddel tegen het speen (treatment for 'weaning' (?) or teething complaints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of honey at meals is said to have cured severe cases of 'speen' (likely scrofula or teething ailments). (L'Abeille et la Ruche.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short note claiming dietary honey has remedial effects for a particular condition; specifics sparse.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18º Geneesmiddel voor zeere en ontsteken oogen (for sore and inflamed eyes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix one part honey with five parts water and wash eyelids 2–3 times daily, ensuring some drops enter the eye; claims complete cure. (Newman.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical eye wash; implies dilution 1:5; use multiple times daily.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19º Geneesmiddel tegen de mondzweren (oral ulcers in children)
rubrics_metrics.description: Children's mouth sores cured by honey mixed with alum or borax; during teething rub gums with decoction of mallows or flaxseed or saffron solution mixed with honey. (Voirnot.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical use in mouth; specifics include mixing with aluin or borax and using soothing decoctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20º Honigzalf (honey ointment for persistent wounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix two spoons of honey, one egg yolk and enough flour to make a dough. This salve is excellent for old wounds that won't close, bleeding sores and running wounds. (Newman.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipe and topical application instructions for chronic wounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verschillend gebruik des honigs — fruit preservation with honey
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve all kinds of fruit by pouring cold clarified or spun honey over clean, dry, selected fruit in jars until covered by several centimeters; immediately close jars with strong paper. (Le Rucher.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method for preserving fruit in honey; used as an alternative to other preservation means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elzasche peperkoek (Alsatian gingerbread) recipe
rubrics_metrics.description: Ingredients: 1/2 kg yellow honey, 1/2 kg rye flour, 10 g potash. Heat honey and gradually add flour, then potash dissolved in brandy; knead, cut and bake; glaze with sugar and egg white (125 g sugar and 1 egg for the given quantity). (Dennler.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific baking recipe for regional gingerbread using honey; includes glazing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honigkoeken met citroen (honey cakes with lemon) recipe
rubrics_metrics.description: Ingredients: 1 cup butter, 2 cups honey, 4 well‑beaten eggs, small spoon lemon extract, 1/2 cup sour milk, small spoon soda and enough flour to knead; bake on hot stove. (Newman.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recipe for making honey cakes flavored with lemon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grog (honey sweetened grog) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Grog is a drink composed of cognac or rum diluted with cold or warm water and sweetened with honey to taste. (Dennler.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple beverage recipe using honey as sweetener; presented as both pleasant and medicinal in other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chrysomel (honey liqueur) recipe
rubrics_metrics.description: Take 4 kilos honey in water to get 8 liters, boil down to 4 liters; mix with 5 liters pure alcohol in which vanilla pieces were infused 8–15 days to obtain about 7 liters of liqueur. (Voirnot.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure to produce a honey liqueur; gives quantities and stages for maceration and reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chartreuse with honey recipe
rubrics_metrics.description: To make 10 liters: 4 liters alcohol, 100 g chartreuse extract, 3 kg honey, 3–4 liters water, 5 g glue for clarification. Mix alcohol with extract, rest 12 hours, dilute and cook honey with 2 liters water, cool, mix, add glue next day, filter after 14 days. (Dennler.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedure for creating a honey liqueur flavored with chartreuse extract; includes clarification step and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other honey liqueurs (general guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honey liqueurs are made by mixing spirit with strongly boiled honey‑must; aromatics (caraway, mint, kirsch, etc.) are infused in alcohol beforehand; after resting, strain and mix with concentrated honey must. [Footnote referencing Bertrand, Voirnot, Leriche.]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General process for producing various honey liqueurs; references specialized sources for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of honey in veterinary medicine (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honey used in veterinary medicine often yields good effects when mixed with certain medicines; it makes medicines more palatable and improves their effectiveness; many animals willingly take medicated honey mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: used to treat young calves after birth to prevent 'afgang'; mixed with other drugs to treat equine foot disease 'le crapaud'; large‑scale use observed during outbreaks like 'blaarziekte'—farmers obtained honey for treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 1: Verzachtende drank (emollient drink)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ingredients: barley 375 g, water 9 kg, honey 1/2 kg. Make a drink to give in severe constipation. (Apiculture pratique.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: prepare barley infusion/beer‑like drink sweetened with honey; dosing not precisely specified—give in constipation cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 2: Weekmakende drank (softening drink)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ingredients: flaxseed (vlaszaad) 125 g; boiling water 10 liters; honey 125 g. Let cool and give in two doses for constipation. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A laxative drink for animals; two administrations per treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 3: Water‑diuretic drink
rubrics_metrics.description: Ingredients: white wine 4000 g, water 4000 g, saltpeter 90 g, honey 125 g. Give in two or three doses per day. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatments intended as diuretics; dosing frequency indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 4: Sleep drink (sedative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opium 5 centigrams; honey‑water 1500 g. For dosing: used in case of 'afgang' and diarrhea in horses or oxen. (White.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains opium; emphasizes consulting a veterinarian for proper use; indicates dose form and condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 5: Refreshing medicinal drink
rubrics_metrics.description: Honey 150 g; vinegar 75 g; water 100 g. (Apiculture pratique.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple refreshing tonic for animals; proportions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 6: Worm‑expelling mixture for horse
rubrics_metrics.description: Terpentine spirit 30 g; 3–4 egg yolks; honey 200 g; water or white wine 1000 g. Beat yolks with terpentine spirit and honey and add to wine. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthelmintic preparation for equines; caution implied—consult vet.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 7: Ergot‑based uterine remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Powdered ergot (moederkoren) 30 g; red wine 1000 g; honey 250 g. In such diseases consult the veterinarian. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious remedy requiring professional oversight; explicit veterinary consultation recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 8: Zalf (ointment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take honey and rye flour, make into a dough and apply to hooves in case of 'spruwkoorts' and to old wounds which will be cleansed and healed. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical hoof and wound application; simple poultice formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 9: Cough‑suppressant opium mixture
rubrics_metrics.description: Licorice powder 30 g; mallow powder 30 g; opium 1 g; honey 300 g. For droes, colds and 'zinkingen'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Powerful mixture including opium; intended for serious respiratory conditions in animals; vet involvement recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 10: Cough pills
rubrics_metrics.description: Ipecac 4 g; camphor 8 g; licorice 15 g; honey in sufficient quantity to make into pills. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulation for making medicated pills for cough; proportions given for active ingredients.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 11: Mouth disease (spruw) wash
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash the mouth with: alum powder 20 g; honey 150 g; vinegar 200 g; water 1000 g. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for mouth lesions in horses/cattle; proportions for wash provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 12: Droes (strangles) remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Spiesglans 40 g; sulfur 100 g; gentian powder 100 g; calamus root 50 g; linseed meal 200 g; honey as needed to make into a lickable paste. Give 3–4 times per day so quantity lasts 4 days. (Wagenfeld.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex internal/external treatment for equine respiratory disease; administer multiple times daily.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 13: Cancerous mouth ulcer (cattle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spanish green (copper acetate) 20 g; honey 50 g; vinegar 500 g. Mix to make a wash. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical wash for severe oral lesions in cattle; contains caustic copper salts—professional vet guidance strongly implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 14: Mouth disease of calves (remedy 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize by refusal to suck and wasting; compose topical mix: Borax 10 g; tincture of myrrh 15 g; honey 40 g. Apply several times daily to raw mouth places. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical application for calf oral lesions; dosing and frequency specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: VEEARTSENIJKUNDE Prescription 15: Mouth disease of calves (remedy 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take elderflowers and sage leaves 50 g each, infuse one hour in 1.5 L boiling water; to strained liquid add 150 g honey and 10 g alum and wash calf's mouth several times a day. (ID.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative herbal wash for calf oral disease; includes honey and alum for antiseptic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aangegeven aanbevelingen (recommended works and periodicals)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of recommended works: e.g., 'Bestier der bieenhalle' by Ed. Bertrand (translated by W.-F. Rondou), 'De gewijzigde Bieënkas Dadant', 'Lessen van Landbouwkunde' by W.-F. Rondou; periodicals: De Bieënvriend and Revue Internationale d'Apiculture with subscription prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References and further reading for beekeeping and honey products; includes publishers, editions, and subscription information — useful for further study and authoritative recipes/techniques.
